LESSON: READING 2.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: LITERARY AND NONLITERARY TEXTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading: literary and nonliterary texts
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading: literary and nonliterary texts, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one carefully select the text to read? 2 What do we consider when selecting a text to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. preview varied texts such as online or offline newspapers, magazines and periodicals, novels and narratives among others. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or 1

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading: literary and nonliterary texts together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn as the learner works independently as they select a suitable text from a collection of online/offline

newspapers, magazines and periodicals with information on the environment.

● Citizenship as the learner engages effectively with others as they relate the information from a text to events, persons

and places in real life.

Values

● Patriotism is promoted as a learner exhibits honesty as they prepare and compare reading logs with peers.

● Integrity is enhanced as a learner portrays self-discipline as they preview varied texts such as online/offline

newspapers, magazines and periodicals, novels, collections of narratives among others.
